# 3.2 - Marginal and Conditional Distributions {.unnumbered}

| | **Job** | **No job** | **Total** |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Sport** | 8 | 22 | 30 |
| **No sport** | 12 | 18 | 30 |
| **Total** | 20 | 40 | 60 |

Do students who play a sport have jobs as often as students who do not? 8 students who play a sport have a job. 12 students who do not play a sport have a job. These counts do not answer the question. You need percents **inside each group**.

In this lesson, you find {{< glink "marginal distribution" text="marginal" >}} and {{< glink "conditional distribution" text="conditional" >}} distributions. Then you use them to decide if two variables are {{< glink slug="association" text="associated" >}}.

:::{.objectives}
- [ ] I find a marginal distribution.
- [ ] I find a conditional distribution.
- [ ] I choose the right total to divide by.
- [ ] I decide if two categorical variables are associated.
:::

{{< glink "conditional distribution" >}},

{{< learn >}}

### 3.2.1 - Marginal and Conditional

| | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Marginal distribution** | Percents from the **totals** (the margins). Divide by the **grand total**. | Job: $\frac{20}{60} \approx 33\%$. No job: $\frac{40}{60} \approx 67\%$. |
| **Conditional distribution** | Percents inside **one group**. Divide by that group's **total**. | Students who play a sport. Job: $\frac{8}{30} \approx 27\%$. No job: $\frac{22}{30} \approx 73\%$. |

:::{.gotcha title="Check the denominator"}
"Of the students who **play a sport**, what percent have a job?"

Divide by the sport total (30). Do not divide by 60. Do not divide by the job total (20).
:::

:::{.you-try title="Of the students who do NOT play a sport, what percent have a job?"}
The group is "No sport." Its total is 30.

$\frac{12}{30} = 40\%$
:::

***

### 3.2.2 - Association

Compare the conditional distributions of the two groups. A {{< glink "segmented bar chart" >}} shows them side by side.

![](/images/Unit_3/3.2_bars_sport_job.svg){width="380px" fig-align="center"}

- Sport: about 27% have a job.
- No sport: 40% have a job.

The percents are **different**. So playing a sport and having a job are **associated**. In this group, students who play a sport are less likely to have a job.

:::{.remember title="Association"}
- Conditional percents are **different** in the groups: the variables are **associated**.
- Conditional percents are about the **same**: there is **no association**.
:::

:::{.think title="Does this mean sports cause students to not have jobs?"}
We cannot tell from this table. An association only says the two things happen together. It does not prove cause. Maybe practice takes time away from a job. Maybe something else explains both. You will learn more about cause in Unit 5.
:::

{{< practice >}}

Work with a partner. Compare answers when you finish each problem.

Problems 1 to 4 use this table of how 80 students get to school.

| | **Bus** | **Car** | **Walk** | **Total** |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **9th grade** | 18 | 12 | 10 | 40 |
| **10th grade** | 14 | 20 | 6 | 40 |
| **Total** | 32 | 32 | 16 | 80 |

**Marginal and Conditional**

1. Find the marginal distribution of how students get to school.

2. Conditional distributions:

   a. Find the conditional distribution of how 9th graders get to school.

   b. Find the conditional distribution of how 10th graders get to school.

   c. Is grade associated with how students get to school? Explain.

3. Denominators:

   a. What percent of 10th graders come by car?

   b. What percent of car riders are 10th graders?

   c. Why are the answers to (a) and (b) different?

4. Is each statement a **marginal** or a **conditional** percent?

   a. 40% of all students ride the bus.

   b. Of the students who walk, 62.5% are 9th graders.

   c. Half of the students are 10th graders.

   d. 25% of 9th graders walk.

***

**Association**

5. 100 students said if they wear glasses and if they play an instrument.

   | | **Glasses** | **No glasses** | **Total** |
   |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
   | **Instrument** | 12 | 28 | 40 |
   | **No instrument** | 18 | 42 | 60 |
   | **Total** | 30 | 70 | 100 |

   a. What percent of students who play an instrument wear glasses?

   b. What percent of students who do not play an instrument wear glasses?

   c. Is playing an instrument associated with wearing glasses? Explain.

6. This segmented bar chart shows the conditional distributions from problem 2.

   ![](/images/Unit_3/3.2_bars_transport.svg){width="380px"}

   a. Which grade has the larger percent of students who walk?

   b. How does the chart show that grade and transportation are associated?
